question: By selling an article at frac{2}7 of its original selling price, Manav incurs a loss of 24%. If he sells the article at 55% of its original selling price, find the profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100%.

Selling at 2/7 of SP gives a 24% loss, meaning 2/7 of SP = 76% of CP.

Original SP = 76% × (7 ÷ 2) = 266% of CP.

New Selling Price = 55% of Original SP = 55% of 266% = 146.3% of CP.

Profit % = 146.3% − 100% = 46.3%.

**∴ The correct answer is 46.3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss percentage when sold at 2/7 of Original SP = 24%

New Selling Price = 55% of Original SP

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP − SP

Profit % = [(New SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 Profit = 146.3% − 100% = 46.3%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) be 100x.

⇒ Loss = 24% of CP = 24x

⇒ Selling Price at 24% loss = 100x − 24x = 76x

⇒ We are given that this Selling Price is 2/7 of Original SP.

⇒ (2 ÷ 7) × Original SP = 76x

⇒ Original SP = (76x × 7) ÷ 2

⇒ Original SP = 38x × 7 = 266x

⇒ The new selling price is 55% of Original SP.

⇒ New SP = (55 ÷ 100) × 266x = 1.463 × 100x = 146.3x

⇒ Since New SP (146.3x) > CP (100x), there is a profit.

⇒ Profit = 146.3x − 100x = 46.3x

⇒ Profit % = (46.3x ÷ 100x) × 100 = 46.3%

**∴ The correct answer is 46.3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). Profit = SP − CP.

Loss Percentage

Loss is calculated directly on the Cost Price. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Marked Price (MP) is the price printed on the article, and discount is always calculated on the MP. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.
